title: Implement append-only Telegram callback navigation
evidence_required: FT-002-AC-001 — RED: captured authorized navigation/mutation callbacks currently issue editMessageText before a late answerCallbackQuery, while unauthorized and wrong-group callbacks emit answerCallbackQuery rejection output. GREEN: private and target-chat authorized navigation/mutation traces begin with answerCallbackQuery and then send one applicable fresh menu/state from current settings; old-menu actions use current persisted settings, unauthorized and wrong-group traces have zero settings mutation and zero Bot API requests, invalid authorized callbacks retain bounded append-only rejection feedback, and owned traces have zero editMessageText. Decisive comparison: ordered methods change from edit-before-ack and unauthorized rejection output to authorized [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage] and unauthorized/wrong-group [], while Backend before/after state distinguishes permitted mutations. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-002-AC-002 RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: the baseline already persists valid price, negative-word, and interval input through the Backend, clears only the submitting administrator/chat pending key, and sends a fresh main menu, so observing claim absence would require breaking preserved behavior; alternative proof: capture pre-change GREEN for all three modes and cross-admin/cross-chat isolation, then claim-equivalent post-change GREEN. Decisive comparison: settings values, pending-key state, destination chat, sendMessage count, and zero editMessageText remain equivalent before and after, with no mutation by a different administrator/chat. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.

FT-002-AC-004 / REQ-006 RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: the baseline contains none of the forbidden client detection, edit retry/cache, old-message deletion, persistence/configuration/dependency/worker/compatibility machinery, and observing RED would require introducing a forbidden mechanism; alternative proof: capture pre-change production-path, dependency, configuration, persistence, runtime-call, and owner inventory, then compare the post-change diff and required native build. Decisive comparison: go.mod/go.sum, internal/config, internal/store, changed production paths, Telegram method call sites, and boundary ownership show only reuse of the existing Bot, Backend settings, pending map, renderers, sendMessage, and answerCallbackQuery, while ./scripts/build.sh passes. Artifact: .tasks/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1/TASK-002-T3-FT-002-W1-acceptance-evidence.md.
purpose: Make authorized callback navigation and filter mutation visible across Telegram clients through prompt acknowledgement and fresh current-state messages while preserving authorization and existing text-input isolation.
success_outcome: Authorized private/target-chat navigation and mutation callbacks are acknowledged first and produce fresh current-state messages with zero edits; unauthorized and wrong-group callbacks are silent and non-mutating, and all valid text-input modes retain isolated persistence and fresh main-menu output without new machinery.
anti_goals: Do not implement manual-scan start/completion/error feedback owned by TASK-003-T2-FT-002-W1.
Do not add client detection, edit retry/cache, old-message deletion, compatibility machinery, persistence, schema, configuration, dependency, worker, profile, or group support.
Do not change the administrator allowlist, private/target-chat authorization decision, Telegram offset durability, shared settings ownership, or pending-key identity.
Do not change Polling Application production behavior, FT-001 polling behavior, or FT-003 publication/deployment behavior.
Do not remove or redesign the generic Telegram client edit API; the required outcome is zero edit requests from the owned runtime flows.

forbidden_scope: manual-scan start/completion/error implementation owned by TASK-003-T2-FT-002-W1
internal/app production polling, scheduling, backoff, and state-transition behavior
internal/store schema, paths, or stored-row interpretation
administrator allowlist and target-chat authorization policy
stop_conditions: A required production change cannot stay inside the accepted Telegram Adapter owner and current Backend contract.

Execution requires changing manual-scan feedback, authorization policy, pending-key identity, scheduler ownership, polling lifecycle, Telegram offset durability, SQLite, configuration, dependency graph, or production runtime.
Execution requires a project path outside the hard write boundary, excluding workflow-owned evidence and lifecycle bookkeeping.
Execution reveals an unresolved product behavior, public contract, data authority, tier, dependency, or task-boundary decision.
Any authorization-boundary probe cannot run in the disposable in-memory Backend and local httptest harness with safe rerun and no external side effect.
Execution cannot obtain honest claim-linked RED/GREEN or accepted alternative proof for FT-002-AC-001, FT-002-AC-002, and FT-002-AC-004.

constraints: Keep one Go modular monolith and the accepted package dependency graph.
Acknowledge an authorized navigation/mutation callback before its action and send the resulting current state as a fresh message without an edit request.
Keep old menus actionable against current persisted settings without deleting or caching old messages.
Keep pending price, negative-word, and interval input in the existing map keyed by administrator and chat and persist only through the existing Backend.
Keep manual-scan feedback outside this task while preserving compatibility with its existing callback branch.
Use only the isolated existing httptest and in-memory Backend harness; no live Telegram, Somon, SQLite, or production probe is authorized.
The non-empty write boundary is hard; the native build gate may write only its exact two listed dist artifacts.
invariants: Authorized private/target-chat navigation and mutation callbacks are acknowledged promptly; unauthorized users and wrong group chats neither mutate settings nor emit bot output.
Owned callback results and valid text-input completion use new messages and make no runtime editMessageText request.
The newest bot message represents current settings/state; an old menu action reads and mutates current persisted settings.
Pending input remains isolated by administrator and chat and clears only after valid persistence or explicit cancellation.
No client detection, edit retry/cache, deletion, persistence, schema, configuration, dependency, worker, compatibility layer, profile, group, or duplicate owner is added.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-001: isolated Bot API traces and Backend state for authorized private/target-chat, stale-menu, unauthorized, wrong-group, and invalid-callback cases prove prompt acknowledgement order, fresh current-state output, boundary isolation, and zero edits in owned flows.
FT-002-AC-002: all three valid input modes plus cross-admin and cross-chat scenarios prove settings persistence, exact pending-key isolation/clearance, one fresh main menu, and zero edits.

FT-002-AC-004 / REQ-006: pre/post dependency, configuration, persistence, runtime-call, changed-path, and owner review plus ./scripts/build.sh prove the forbidden mechanisms and duplicate owners remain absent.

T3 safety: every authorization probe uses only the in-process Bot, disposable Backend, and local httptest server; it is safely rerunnable, makes no external request, and records request/state isolation.
